english: It comes and no one leads her. It calls the field and the house (home). Her sun hides. What is it? Night.
uncertain: ḱéleti 'calls' vs ḱéletor 'hides' (kelh1- vs ḱel-) - read the active as 'calls (in)' and the middle as 'hides'

english: What, sister, goes and does not leave its own bed? It goes (out) from the earth. Wild beasts drink it. What is it? A stream.
uncertain: linkʷtés is not a form I recognise for *leykʷ- 'leave' (expected nasal present linékʷti); read as 'leaves'
dʰǵʰmés read as gen./abl. 'from the earth'; tód 'that' as subject

english: A sheep slipped into a trap. Then a wild beast came. The sheep said: 'Beast, free (?) me. I will give you a gift.' Then the beast split the trap and freed (?) her. Then the beast lay down. Then a man came. Then the sheep saw the man and cried out. Then the beast awoke and fled. The sheep said: 'I have given you a gift.'
uncertain: spr̥dʰí / spért: *sper- 'kick/jerk' - read as 'free/release', meaning unclear

english: Dawn gave cattle to the man who works. Dawn did not give cattle to the son lying in bed. It has dawned. Man, stand up!

The wolf clothed himself in wool and went at the sheep. Then the mouse saw the teeth. The mouse said: 'Sheep, look! One is not a sheep. The wool is a garment, the teeth are his own.' Then the wolf took fright and fled. The wool calls the wolf (in?), and the teeth make him known.
uncertain: last sentence: 'the wool calls/ hides the wolf' - ḱéleti ambiguous (call vs hide)

english: Where there is smoke, there is fire. Smoke goes up out of the house. Fire does not hide.
